A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Draw-and-Understand, its visual prompt encoder, training data, and benchmarks. The main text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring and renaming.

before.justification: v1 reports original SPHINX-V benchmark results and ablations, including Visual Genome captioning and VCR reasoning results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 reports original VP-SPHINX and VP-LLaVA evaluations, expanded ablations, and VCR reasoning results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: v3 adds a concrete LLaVA-based implementation using CLIP-ViT-L/14 and LLaMA3-8B alongside the SPHINX/MoV-LLaMA2 models. This extends the model architecture choices, but the visual prompt encoder, two-stage training schedule, and conversion of free-form prompts into boxes remain essentially unchanged. The framework renaming itself is not a new algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds remote-sensing training coverage and broadens stage-2 training from whole-image captions to general image question answering and reasoning. Table 2 adds VQAv2, MME perception, POPE, SEED, TextVQA, and DocVQA evaluations. The Visual Genome captioning evaluation in v1 Appendix B.1 is removed, although Visual Genome remains training data.

E2.justification: Comparator membership changes substantially across retained experiments. v3 adds Ferret-v2 to LVIS and Ferret-Bench, and adds original SPHINX-X and Osprey comparisons to Ferret-Bench. It removes Kosmos-2 and Ferret-7B from the classification comparisons and omits several RefCOCOg comparators, including GRIT and GLaMM. New general-image evaluations also compare against Qwen-VL and LLaVA-Next.

E3.justification: The reported image processing changes from fixed 448-by-448 preprocessing to each backbone's dynamic-resolution strategy, and maximum sequence length increases from 2048 to 3072. Proposed-model evaluations expand from one 13B configuration to 7B, 8B, and 13B configurations. Reported MDVP size changes from approximately 0.9 million images and 1.6 million examples to 0.8 million images and 1.2 million examples, alongside revised training-mixture counts.

E4.justification: v1 Table 9 tests prompt representation and one-stage versus two-stage training on LVIS/PACO. v3 Table 4 adds a substantive data-source ablation comparing Grounding-QA-only, GPT-4V-only, and combined data, and extends the existing ablations to OCR and MDVP-Bench. Qualitative comparisons also change: v1 Figure 6's competitor examples disappear, while v3 Figure 5 compares VP-SPHINX and VP-LLaVA responses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed protocols, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both present point estimates; additional result rows do not change this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Many results are added, removed, or revised. Corresponding 13B SPHINX entries change from 55.04 to 51.32 for PACO semantic IoU, 92.19 to 88.19 for detailed RefCOCOg captioning, and 89.63 to 80.65 for VCR Q-to-AR accuracy. PACO semantic IoU now trails Osprey's 52.72. v3 adds results for new model configurations, image-level benchmarks, and data ablations. Revised training settings prevent interpreting these replacements as controlled performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Neither version develops substantive formal theory, theorems, or proofs. Changes to architectural notation and explanations do not introduce or revise mathematical results.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on the SPHINX-V model and fine-grained visual prompting. v3's abstract, introduction, and conclusion instead claim a general framework adaptable to multiple pretrained MLLMs, with preservation of original image-level perception as an explicit central objective. This broadens the scientific contribution beyond renaming the model.

C2.justification: v1 attributes weaker image-level performance to the absence of image-level VQA training. v3 acknowledges remaining degradation relative to original backbones despite adding such data, partly attributing it to using only a subset of instruction data. It also interprets the new data ablation as evidence for GPT-4V data's complementary value and omits v1's explicit claim that two-stage training accelerates convergence.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix A and Table 7 newly disclose batch sizes, epochs, warmup, cosine scheduling, gradient clipping, and weight decay. It also specifies Gaussian box perturbations and implementation details for the additional backbone. These are useful disclosures, not evidence that every setting changed. Conversely, v1's explicit 512-dimensional prompt-encoder output is no longer stated. Most data-generation templates and the project URL are retained.

R1.justification: v3 substantially repositions the work as a reusable adaptation framework, contrasting it with architecture-specific methods, costly training from scratch, and approaches that neglect global perception. It adds literature supporting the expanded scope, including Ferret-v2, LLaMA3, GeoChat, remote-sensing datasets, and general-image benchmarks. Moving related work to the appendix is separate from these substantive positioning changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method narrative are extensively rewritten around VP-MLLMs. The dataset discussion is reorganized into multi-target captioning and instruction conversations, related work moves from the main text to Appendix B, experimental subsections are merged, and implementation material is reorganized. SPHINX-V and MDVP-Data terminology is systematically replaced.

P2.justification: v3 consolidates several separate classification, captioning, and benchmark tables into larger combined displays. Figure 4 incorporates the prompt-encoder diagram previously in v1's appendix; Figure 6 adds training-data preprocessing illustrations; qualitative displays are replaced or redesigned. Training-data tables move to the appendix, and the document adopts a substantially different conference layout.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens empirical support through a second backbone family, comparisons with original models on broader image-level tasks, and a direct ablation of GPT-4V-generated data (Tables 2-4). These address gaps in v1's evidence for generality and data utility, while Table 7 supplies missing training details. The removed Visual Genome comparison and overstated PACO superiority language reduce completeness and precision, but the stronger validation and reproducibility information provide a substantial net improvement.
